versions.label: Douay-Rheims
versions.blurb: The English of the Vulgate itself: translated from Jerome’s Latin, so it follows the Vulgate verse for verse.

versions.label: King James
versions.long: King James Version (1611; 1769 text) with Apocrypha
versions.blurb: The Bible of the English-speaking Reformation, translated from Hebrew and Greek. Its 1611 edition included the deuterocanonical books as “Apocrypha”.

versions.label: World English
versions.blurb: A modern, plain-English translation from the Hebrew and Greek, in the public domain, with the deuterocanon.

versions.label: JPS Tanakh
versions.blurb: The Hebrew Bible as Jewish scholars rendered it, from the Masoretic text — the reading Jesus’ own people give the Old Testament. Old Testament only; writes the divine name as “G-d”.

versions.label: Berean
versions.blurb: A fresh, readable modern-English translation from the Hebrew and Greek, released into the public domain in 2023 — the closest free equivalent to the ESV or NIV. Protestant canon (66 books).

versions.label: Catholic PDV
versions.blurb: A modern-English translation of the Latin Vulgate itself by Ronald Conte — the Douay-Rheims brought into today’s language, with all 73 books.

versions.label: Septuagint
versions.blurb: The Old Testament as the apostles quoted it — Sir Lancelot Brenton's English of the Greek Septuagint, with the Psalms in their Greek numbering, the Song of the Three, Susanna and Bel in Daniel, and the Letter of Jeremiah in Baruch. Old Testament only.

versions.label: Reina-Valera
versions.blurb: La Biblia en español — the classic Spanish Bible of Casiodoro de Reina and Cipriano de Valera in its 1909 revision, public domain. Protestant canon.

versions.label: Greek NT
versions.blurb: The New Testament in its own Greek — the SBL Greek New Testament edited by Michael Holmes — with Strong’s numbers on every word. Tap a word for its meaning and every other place it appears.

versions.label: Hebrew OT
versions.blurb: The Old Testament in Hebrew, from the Leningrad Codex (AD 1008), the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible, with Strong’s numbers on every word. Hebrew numbering, laid on the Vulgate grid.
